reason: The cited evidence does not address laser cladding of Inconel 718, its effect on hot cracking, or comparative fatigue/wear performance. E1 discusses arc welding of CoCrFeNiCux alloys, E2 concerns a different FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating on H13 steel, and E3 only introduces laser cladding generally for H13 steel without supporting the specific mechanism or predicted outcome. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Laser cladding's low heat input minimizes substrate melting and prevents segregation of low-melting phases that cause hot cracking.
Rapid solidification in laser cladding produces a refined, uniform microstructure that improves residual stress distribution.
Inconel 718 can be deposited as a thin, metallurgically bonded layer via laser cladding with minimal dilution.
The proposed laser-clad repair will improve fatigue life by 20–30% and high-temperature wear resistance compared to fusion welding.
Traditional fusion welding of the target material leads to hot cracking due to low-melting phases and wide solidification ranges.
